proposal.hypothesis: Starting from the current best measured configuration, increase only wheel_radius_ratio from 0.27531120025870004 to 0.29531120025870004, a two-step advisory increment above the suspected prior radius probe, while keeping side_m, print_mass_ref_kg, wheel_mass_kg, inner_radius_ratio, wheel_thickness_m, and all controller scales identical. Expected mechanism: a larger effective wheel radius raises the wheel’s axial rotational inertia at unchanged wheel mass, so the same body angular-momentum disturbance requires a smaller wheel angular velocity. This should directly reduce the recurring speed_governor_fraction violation without relying on extra rotating mass, which could otherwise worsen hold stability, drift, or torque demand. Evidence for success would be speed_governor_fraction falling toward or below the 0.01 screening limit while status remains completed and peak_tilt_deg, final_1s_tilt_rms_deg, peak_pivot_displacement_mm, contact_fraction, peak_slip_speed_m_s, and continuous_torque_exceeded_fraction do not materially regress relative to the current best score of 0.9074724957694985. If stability or drift degrades despite improved speed margin, that would indicate the larger radius changes contact kinematics or effective leverage enough to offset the inertia benefit.
